speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; please describe your current symptoms of increasing pain and swelling in the right knee, and tell me about the episodes of pain with urination. You also mentioned a history of a painful, swollen left ankle; when did that occur and how long did it last?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome). The patient presents with the classic triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and risk factors including new sexual activity and inconsistent condom use.
